product_family: Consumer real-time AI voice changer and soundboard (desktop app + Voicemod Key mobile companion + Voicelab voice creation tool), plus a separate developer offering (Control API, Cloud API, and embeddable SDK for third-party apps/games).

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type I/II)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. No trust center, security page, or SOC 2 mention found on voicemod.net (homepage, privacy policy, or terms of use); privacy policy only offers a general assurance of 'top-notch admin, technical, and physical safeguards' with no named framework.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not referenced anywhere on voicemod.net.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence; not applicable to a consumer voice-changer/soundboard product, and not claimed anywhere on the vendor's site.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a vendor-held PCI DSS attestation; purchases route through store.voicemod.net, consistent with reliance on a third-party payment processor rather than a vendor-held PCI certification.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not a government/enterprise-cloud oriented product.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of ISO 42001. Not to be confused with the 'Fairly Trained' certification below, which covers training-data sourcing ethics, not an AI management-system standard.

certifications.name: Fairly Trained (AI training-data ethics certification, non-security)
certifications.proof_quote: AI voices trained with pro voice actors / Fairly Trained certified models.

privacy.ai_training_note: Privacy policy states: 'we do not listen to your conversations when you are using the real-time voice changer features in VM Products and we do not listen to any voice recordings you provide for the purposes of AI voice creation.' Voice-sample based training only occurs through an opt-in 'voice improvement projects' program requiring active consent. Separately, the Community Hub content license in the Terms of Use grants Voicemod a broad license to 'perform, prepare derivative works of, incorporate into other works or otherwise exploit' user-submitted content, which is a wider reuse right than the privacy policy's training language covers, so treat community-uploaded content and private voice/AI-creation data as governed by different rules. No dedicated Data Processing Agreement (DPA) was found published on the site.
privacy.data_region: Company seated in Valencia, Spain; privacy policy states servers/cloud providers (Google, AWS) are 'all around the globe and mostly in Europe,' with possible processing in the UK and other supplier jurisdictions.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: n/a - not verified. Not documented on any vendor-domain page found.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: n/a - not verified. Privacy policy makes only a general, unspecific claim of 'necessary security measures... admin, technical, and physical safeguards' with no technical detail.

security.name: Formal security disclosures
security.value: None found. No trust center, security.txt, or dedicated security page located on voicemod.net.

security.name: Terms of Use security disclaimer
security.value: Terms of Use explicitly disclaim absolute security: electronic systems 'do not offer absolute guarantees of security,' and users are advised not to rely on the service for 'confidential, secret, critical or reserved information.'

security.name: Minimum age / minors
security.value: Service usable from age 16, with parental consent required above that threshold per the stated policy.

products.name: Voicemod Voice Changer / Soundboard (desktop app)

products.data_scope: Installs a local virtual microphone; real-time voice processing runs locally per the privacy policy ('we do not listen to your conversations...using the real-time voice changer features')
products.notes: Free tier plus paid subscription; main flagship consumer product.

products.name: Voicelab
products.data_scope: User-mixed voice effects; AI voice creation feature is opt-in for any training use of submitted voice recordings.

products.name: Voicemod Key
products.category: Mobile companion app for console voice-changing control
products.notes: Pairs phone with console to unlock voice changer/soundboard features.

products.name: Voicemod Control API
products.data_scope: Remote-controls the locally installed Voicemod desktop app; per the developer page, does not require cloud access.
products.notes: For third-party apps/games that want to trigger effects in the local Voicemod app.

products.name: Voicemod Cloud API / SDK
products.category: Developer/embeddable API and SDK (cloud, incl. Speech-to-Speech)
products.data_scope: Developer page marks this offering as 'Requires Cloud Access,' implying audio is processed on Voicemod's cloud infrastructure for this product; no public documentation found on this offering's specific data retention, encryption, or regional handling.
products.notes: Distinct data-handling profile from the desktop app; treat as a materially different trust posture pending vendor confirmation. Partnerships referenced include Switchboard Audio SDK integration.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium (free desktop app + paid Pro subscription; separate commercial terms for developer/enterprise API and SDK use)
compare.data_residency: Primarily EU (Spain-seated entity), with cloud processing via AWS and Google described as 'mostly in Europe' and possible processing in additional supplier jurisdictions including the UK

flags: No trust center, security page, or named security framework (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA) found anywhere on voicemod.net; absence is based on a thorough search of the privacy policy, terms of use, homepage, and developer page rather than a confirmed 'in scope, not certified' statement from the vendor, so treat as 'no public evidence' rather than a definitive denial.

The 'Fairly Trained' badge shown prominently on the homepage ('AI voices trained with pro voice actors. Fairly Trained certified models.') is a training-data ethics/licensing certification from a third-party nonprofit, not a security or AI-governance-management-system certification (e.g. not ISO/IEC 42001 or CSA STAR AI). Do not list it as a security cert on the AIFOXX listing; label it distinctly as an AI-training-ethics badge.

Cloud API/SDK product ('Requires Cloud Access') has a materially different data-handling profile than the desktop app (which processes audio locally), but no vendor documentation on the Cloud API's data retention, encryption, or regional storage was found. Flag as a gap for enterprise/developer buyers evaluating that specific product.

Community Hub content license in the Terms of Use grants Voicemod broad rights to 'exploit' user-submitted content, which is broader than the privacy policy's narrower 'we do not train on your voice recordings by default' language; the two documents should be read together, not interchangeably.

Search results surfaced other domains (thevoicemod.com, voicemod.us) presenting themselves as 'Voicemod' with their own privacy policy and terms pages; these were NOT used as evidence in this assessment because the evidence file and Voicemod's own legal hub point to voicemod.net as the official domain. Recommend a follow-up identity check before AIFOXX links to any Voicemod page other than voicemod.net or its documented subdomains (support.voicemod.net, control-api.voicemod.net, cloud-api.voicemod.net, store.voicemod.net).
No Data Processing Agreement (DPA) found published on the site; B2B/developer customers who need one should be flagged to contact Voicemod directly to confirm availability.
